facts: The source compares PO/CO2 copolymerization with phosphine/Et3B and with PA added. A representative source feed is [PO]/[PA]/[(Et2N)3P]/[Et3B]=2000/1/1/2, neat,80 °C,initial CO2 pressure2.0 MPa. Separate stoichiometric interaction experiments use TFPO as an epoxide probe and sodium ethoxide as a chain-end probe in stated NMR solvents. These probes and short molecular models are not actual long growing polymer chains. Neither a unique reactive adduct nor a propagation/backbiting barrier is given as a public fact.
scope: Address the source local molecular interaction question using (Et2N)3P, phthalic anhydride (PA), Et3B, propylene oxide (PO) and CO2. Source probe identities and interaction measurements are available; their use is a research decision. Define any adduct, association or chain-end model explicitly and justify its representativeness. Bulk polymer molecular weight, productivity, a complete polymerization network and extrapolation to other catalyst families are outside scope.

limitations: Source-coordinate limitation: SI physical pp39-40 lists 51 atoms (C14H30N3O3P) for the PA adduct; the complete stoichiometric (Et2N)3P + PA model has 61 atoms (C20H34N3O3P), a C6H4 difference. The complete PA reagent connectivity in systems.json remains valid. Reconstruction must identify retained source atoms, added atoms and the resulting graph; a reconstructed model is not an unchanged source geometry. No missing coordinates are supplied or invented here. For main physical p8 Figure 6 and p10, distinguish a specified H-site ADCH population, the nearest-contact H and a declared alpha/beta-H family statistic. Define sites from the N-ethyl CH2/CH3 graph and map them explicitly; do not equate a figure-labelled H with a nearest site or family mean without evidence. Report signed electrostatic potential with its units and surface definition separately from electron density; source colour/prose alone is not a density measurement. These local observables do not by themselves establish polymer propagation or backbiting rates.
